ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=x+b$ intersects the $x$-axis at point $C(4,0)$ and the $y$-axis at point $B$, and intersects the hyperbola $y=\frac{m}{x}$ (where $x<0$) at point $A(-1,n)$. Connect $OA$. What is the area of $\triangle OAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since point $B$ passes through the y-axis,\\
$ \therefore x=0$,\\
$ \therefore y=-4$,\\
$ \therefore {S}_{\triangle AOC}={S}_{\triangle AOB}+{S}_{\triangle BOC}$,\\
$ =\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 1+\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 4$,\\
$ =\boxed{10}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin; a straight line with positive slope intersects the x-axis at point C on the right side, and intersects the y-axis at point B below; there is a branch of a hyperbola in the lower left, and the straight line and the hyperbola intersect near the third quadrant at point A; line segment OA has been connected. Reasoning: According to the given information, C(4,0) is on the straight line y=x+b, so 0=4+b, obtaining b=-4, therefore the equation of the straight line is y=x-4. The abscissa of point A is -1, and A is on this straight line, so n=-1-4=-5, namely A=(-1,-5). In triangle OAC, OC is on the x-axis, with length 4; the distance from point A to the x-axis is |-5|=5. Therefore the area is (1/2)×4×5=10.
